Athletic groin protectors (protective cups) are classified in heading 9506, which covers articles and equipment for general physical exercise, gymnastics, athletics, and other sports. Within 9506.91 (articles and equipment for general physical exercise, gymnastics or athletics), the protective cups would most likely fall under 9506.99, which covers other sports equipment.

I recall that CBP rulings on athletic cups classify them in 9506.99.2580 (other sports equipment, not elsewhere specified, "Other"). Subheading 9506.99.25 covers "Baseball, cricket, lacrosse, and polo equipment, except balls, and parts and accessories thereof," whereas 9506.99.20 covers "Other, Baseball..." and 9506.99.60 covers "Other." So 9506.99.2580 does not fit well for an MMA cup.

HTSUS 9506.99: 9506.99.05 covers "Racket sports..."; 9506.99.10 covers "Basketball..."; 9506.99.15 covers "Cricket"; 9506.99.20 covers "Field hockey"; 9506.99.25 covers "Lacrosse and polo"; 9506.99.30 covers "Baseball"; 9506.99.35 covers "Other." On this basis, 9506.99.60 is the best fit as the general "Other" category. In the current schedule 9506.99.60 is "Other," and its statistical suffixes are 9506.99.6080 (other).

Ruling NY N-series for athletic cups for MMA: 9506.99.6080 seems plausible.
